name: Buff-throated Warbler
rangeDescription: Alpine scrub of central and southern china to southeastern tibet
description: A very plain small warbler without wingbars. Olive-green above with a yellow-washed pale belly and a thin yellowish brow stripe that is strongest above the eye.

name: Blue Petrel
rangeDescription: Islands in subantarctic southern oceans and islands off cape horn
description: Rather small, attractively patterned petrel of cold subantarctic waters; not seen from mainland. Sometimes accompanies ships, especially near breeding islands and with groups of similar-sized and superficially similar prions.

name: Seychelles Sunbird
rangeDescription: Seychelles
description: A drab brown sunbird with a long downcurved bill. Breeding male has a bib of iridescent blue feathers.

name: Nocturnal Curassow
rangeDescription: Humid southern venezuela to northeastern peru and western amazonian brazil
description: This small curassow is entirely warm brown with a bright orange bill, yellow skin above the eye, and gray skin below the eye. True to its name, it is strictly nocturnal and thus extremely difficult to see.

name: White-lored Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to the guianas, northern bolivia, and amazonian and eastern brazil
description: Small flycatcher of rainforest canopy. Olive with bright white or buffy wing bars and a gray head.

name: Dark-throated Seedeater
rangeDescription: Southeastern bolivia (southeastern tarija), southwestern brazil (western mato grosso do sul, southern rio grande do sul), paraguay, northern argentina (salta eastward to corrientes, southward to tucumán, northern córdoba and northern buenos aires), and westerm uruguay; non-breeding to northern and eastern bolivia and central and southern brazil (eastward to minas gerais, and southward to rio grande do sul)
description: A small finchlike bird with a short and stubby bill. Males are a striking combination of gray, black and a rich cinnamon color.

name: Pale-faced Bare-eye
rangeDescription: South-central amazonian brazil (between the rio madeira and rio tapajós, southward to the rio aripuaña)
description: Large antbird, mostly dark olive-brown with black-and-white bars on the chest. Look for the conspicuous white-crested forehead.

name: Fox Kestrel
rangeDescription: Rocky hills and gorges of sub-saharan africa
description: A large kestrel with long pointed wings and tail. The base color is a rich rufous with fine black streaking.

name: Brown-throated Fulvetta
rangeDescription: Himalayas (southeastern tibet to southwestern china, eastern bhutan, and far northeastern india)
description: Orange-brown with black-and-white wing panels and a speckled white “beard” extending down the throat and up to either cheek. Inhabits high-elevation montane forests in the eastern Himalayas, where it usually forages in flocks in dense lower vegetation and in bamboo stands.

name: Long-tailed Fiscal
rangeDescription: Dry thornscrub of southern somalia to kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: A large black-and-white fiscal with a long tail. Note the small white patch at the front of the wing and the white rump, both of which are conspicuous in flight.

name: Yellow-crowned Redstart
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Distinctive warbler endemic to Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. It has a mostly black head, yellow crown and underparts, and a buffy stripe between the eye and bill.

name: Carruthers's Cisticola
rangeDescription: Democratic republic of the congo to uganda, western kenya, rwanda, burundi, and northwestern tanzania
description: Relatively colorful, mid-sized, long-tailed cisticola. Note the gray-brown back with thick black streaks, rufous on the wing and cap, and whitish underparts.

name: Pheasant Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern mexico to brazil, paraguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Very retiring and elusive cuckoo of tropical forest, heard far more often than seen. Sings mainly in spring and summer, and at other times appears absent from areas where it may actually be fairly common.

name: Morotai White-eye
rangeDescription: Morotai (northern moluccas)
description: A tiny warbler-like songbird with a pale eye-ring, endemic to Morotai. Note black head, a broad white eye-ring, a pale forehead line, a pale patch between bill and eye, a gray back, and no yellow below.

name: Flat-billed Vireo
rangeDescription: Semiarid lowland scrub of hispaniola including gonâve island
description: A small, slow-moving species that prefers dry brush and scrublands where it typically feeds low and sometimes even on the ground; sometimes found at higher elevations where it can be found feeding in or near the canopy in vine tangles. The Flat-billed Vireo is a relatively plain species, with bold white wingbars, and whitish eyes.

name: Red-throated Tit
rangeDescription: Acacia savanna of southern kenya and northern tanzania
description: An unusual tit with a rufous face, collar, and breast and a gray cap and back. Also note the prominent white wingbars on the gray wings.

name: Dot-fronted Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Humid andean slopes of southern bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Small greenish woodpecker of the dry and semi-humid forests at the base of the Andes in NW Argentina and southern Bolivia. Male has a red cap, while the female’s head is grayish with pale spots.

name: Amazon Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Southern mexico to colombia, venezuela, and east of andes to argentina
description: Medium-sized kingfisher of tropical lowlands. Found singly or in pairs, along rivers and at the edges of ponds and lakes, often perched on wires or bare snags.

name: Pheasant-tailed Jacana
rangeDescription: Swamps and marshes of india, southeastern asia, and philippines
description: An eye-catching waterbird found on lakes and ponds with extensive floating vegetation. Long-tailed breeding adults are striking: the large white wing patch and head contrast sharply with its black body and bright yellow neck patch.

name: Aztec Rail
rangeDescription: Central mexico
description: Large, chickenlike rail of fresh marshes in highlands. Heard more often than seen; its main call is a rhythmic dry chatter.
